briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for August 30, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Himalayan Catastrophe: A Climate Change Warning
sections.content: A recent unprecedented major flood in Nepal has resulted in severe casualties, with 675 deaths and 2,498 people missing [2]. This is attributed to the weakening of permafrost and increased concerns over the collapse of Himalayan glaciers due to climate change [2, 3, 5]. Specifically, according to Chinese researchers, the area of Himalayan glacial lakes has surged by 27% over the past 30 years, increasing the risk of collapse [21], and experts warn that more glaciers will melt and disasters will increase due to climate change [31]. Such disasters have also put domestic power companies' overseas hydropower projects on high alert [4, 6], and the Nepalese government is strongly urging international efforts to address climate change following the deadly floods [24].

sections.title: 🌱 Expanding Citizen Participation in Domestic Carbon Neutrality Efforts
sections.content: Various efforts are underway domestically to achieve carbon neutrality. Through industry-academia cooperation between Woosuk University and the Korea Climate Change Research Institute, carbon neutrality has been recognized as an issue of practice and data [1], and various local governments are encouraging citizen participation [7]. Siheung City has invested 39.2 million KRW in the Carbon Neutrality Point System, recruiting participants year-round, and achieved a reduction of 2,062 tons of carbon in the first half of the year alone [9, 12, 13]. Furthermore, Nowon-gu conducted a carbon neutrality citizen declaration with 800 participants [10], and Anseong City is strengthening citizen-led carbon neutrality efforts by launching its Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth Committee and Climate Citizen Participation Group [11].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Expansion of Renewable Energy and Practical Challenges
sections.content: Under the 12th Basic Plan for Electricity Supply and Demand, South Korea plans to expand renewable energy sixfold from its current level to 220 GW, with the expansion of power grids and Energy Storage Systems (ESS) identified as key [14]. By 2040, the proportion of renewable energy generation is expected to increase significantly, with 1.5% of the national territory projected to be utilized for solar power plants [17]. However, the 'paradox of the demonstration island' has emerged, where Jeju Island, with a renewable energy share of 65%, is excluded from industrial electricity bill discounts [16]. Furthermore, challenges remain for stable grid operation, such as the implementation of output control to reduce generation when renewable energy output exceeds electricity demand [18]. This domestic situation is contrasted with the United States, where new power facility investments are concentrated in the renewable energy sector, leading to an increase of 83 GW in capacity over one year [15].

sections.title: ⚠️ Widespread Impacts of Climate Change and the Call for International Action
sections.content: Climate change is having widespread impacts beyond specific regions. In heatwave conditions like this year's, cases of pets suffering from heatstroke even indoors have occurred, confirming a threat to life across the board [19]. Research has also been published indicating that 61% of Indian children were exposed to heatwave stress for an additional month due to climate change [36]. In the financial sector, out of 23,424 investment funds totaling 25 trillion USD, only 1.5% align with the 1.5-degree global warming limit target. When supply chain emissions are also considered, no funds meet this target, indicating an urgent need for change in the investment market [30]. The NATO Association emphasizes the need to recognize climate change as a security threat and integrate climate risks into defense policies [32], further highlighting the growing necessity for a global and multifaceted response to climate change [22, 23, 35].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the severe regional disasters and widespread impacts of climate change, while also showcasing domestic and international efforts towards carbon neutrality and the challenges of transitioning to renewable energy. Global cooperation and action to address the climate crisis are more urgent than ever. This concludes today's climate briefing.
